f.title: Meet pharmacovigilance reporting requirements for medicines approved for supply in Australia
f.statement: Sponsors of medicines approved for supply in Australia are legally responsible for meeting the pharmacovigilance reporting requirements for their medicine, in accordance with subsection 28(5)(e) of the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 and Regulation 15A of the Therapeutic Goods Regulations 1990.

f.title: Complete the biennial pharmacovigilance system report via the TGA electronic form
f.statement: One of the sponsor's inspection-related responsibilities is completing a biennial report (once every two years) on its pharmacovigilance system via the electronic form provided, to assist TGA in prioritising inspections.

f.title: Complete the biennial PV system report form when TGA asks; non-completion means the highest risk
f.statement: To help TGA prioritise inspections, TGA will ask the sponsor to complete a biennial report (once every two years) on its pharmacovigilance system via an electronic form made available on the TGA website to all nominated contact persons for pharmacovigilance. The form asks for information on the elements TGA considers when assigning risk (the product, sponsor, pharmacovigilance system and inspection-related factors listed in the guidance); the answers are used to assign the sponsor a risk score from predetermined risk scores, combined with other risk information known to TGA. Sufficient time is given to complete it. The assigned risk score is not made available to the sponsor. If the sponsor does not complete the report, TGA assigns it the highest risk. TGA may also ask the sponsor to complete the form on an ad hoc basis.

rows.actor: Sponsor (sponsor of medicines included on the ARTG)
rows.deadline: Once every two years (biennial), and ad hoc when TGA asks; sufficient time is given (no fixed period stated)
rows.quote: To help us prioritise inspections, we will ask you to complete a biennial report (once every two years) on your pharmacovigilance system via an electronic form made available to all nominated contact persons for pharmacovigilance on the TGA website. The form will ask for information pertaining to the elements we consider when assigning you risk as listed above. Completing the requested fields helps us assign your risk based on predetermined risk scores and prioritise you for inspection. Sufficient time will be given for this survey to be completed. Your risk score obtained from this report will be combined with other risk information known to the TGA in order to prioritise inspections. Your assigned risk score will not be made available to you. If you do not complete the report, we will assign you the highest risk. We may also ask you to complete this form on an ad hoc basis.
rows.review_note: Review: Merged 0011 (consequence: highest risk if not completed; risk score not disclosed) and 0012 (ad hoc requests) into this row; quote now covers the whole paragraph. Level Mandatory: "we will ask you to complete" restates the biennial-report responsibility in 0009, and non-completion has a stated consequence; no "must"/"required" wording. Double-check: level rests on "will ask you" plus the stated consequence, not "must"; overlaps 0009 (same duty, here with the form channel and consequence). Held for human sign-off: reporting clock or deadline.

f.title: Overseas PV sites may be inspected in addition to Australian affiliate sites
f.statement: In most cases TGA limits pharmacovigilance inspections to Australian affiliate sites; however, TGA may also inspect overseas sites if appropriate.
f.clause: Inspection process - Sites to be inspected
f.applicability: Australian affiliate sites and, if appropriate, overseas sites

rows.location: Inspection process - Sites to be inspected
rows.review_note: Review: Kept as a Permitted row on TGA ("we may also inspect overseas sites"): it tells the sponsor that overseas sites are in reach of an inspection, which matters for readiness planning. Actor set to TGA. Double-check: TGA-side permission; whether TGA powers belong in the library is a judgement.

f.title: Contracted PV parties may be inspected, generally arranged through the sponsor
f.statement: Any party or organisation contracted to carry out some or all pharmacovigilance activities in conjunction with, or on behalf of, the sponsor may be inspected to confirm it is capable of supporting the sponsor's compliance with Australian pharmacovigilance obligations. Such inspections will generally be arranged through the sponsor as part of an overall pharmacovigilance inspection.

f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Audit & inspection readiness

Such inspections will generally be arranged through the sponsor as part of an overall pharmacovigilance inspection.

rows.review_note: Review: Kept as Permitted ("may be inspected"); relevant to vendor oversight because such inspections are generally arranged through the sponsor. Actor clarified. Double-check: TGA-side permission; the sponsor's duty to secure the contractor's agreement is in 0005.

f.title: TGA may inspect at any time and, in exceptional circumstances, without notice
f.statement: TGA has the right to perform a pharmacovigilance inspection at any time and, in exceptional circumstances, can perform an inspection without notice; normally TGA gives the sponsor advance notice of its intention to conduct a pharmacovigilance inspection.

rows.quote: We have the right to perform a pharmacovigilance inspection at any time (see Legal basis for pharmacovigilance inspections). In exceptional circumstances, we can perform an inspection without notice. However, we would normally give you advance notice of our intention to conduct a pharmacovigilance inspection.
rows.review_note: Review: Kept as a Permitted row on TGA: the right to inspect at any time, without notice in exceptional circumstances, underlies the readiness duty in 0004. Actor set to TGA. Double-check: TGA-side permission; whether TGA powers belong in the library is a judgement.

f.title: TGA notice period should allow the sponsor to arrange logistics, personnel and data access (guide: 6-8 weeks for routine inspections)
f.statement: The period of notice TGA serves should be sufficient for the sponsor to make logistic arrangements and ensure key personnel are available and have access to relevant data. As a guide, TGA considers six to eight weeks' notice sufficient for a routine inspection.
f.applicability: Announced inspections; the six to eight weeks guide is for routine inspections

rows.actor: TGA (notice of inspection to the sponsor)
rows.deadline: As a guide, six to eight weeks' notice for a routine inspection (TGA's notice period, not a sponsor deadline)

rows.review_note: Review: The "should" applies to the length of TGA's notice, not to the sponsor: actor changed to TGA and the title no longer tells the sponsor to act. f.title: On notification, confirm availability, ensure cooperation, and confirm in writing agreement to inspection of all sites and direct data access
f.statement: When notifying an inspection, TGA will request confirmation of the sponsor's availability, ask the sponsor to ensure the cooperation of all parties, and ask it to confirm in writing that it agrees to the inspection of all relevant sites and will make all required documents and databases directly accessible to TGA inspectors.

f.title: Use the shared inspection plan to make the relevant personnel, rooms, databases and documents available
f.statement: TGA prepares an inspection plan identifying the objectives and scope of the inspection, the inspection team members and their roles, the inspection date and sites, the specific documents, electronic tools and systems to be reviewed and to which TGA requires access (insofar as possible), and the expected time and duration of each major inspection activity. f.title: At the opening meeting, the sponsor may introduce its representatives and present an overview of its PV system
f.statement: The inspection team holds an opening meeting, chaired by the lead inspector, with the sponsor's representatives before the inspection begins. Its purposes include allowing the sponsor to introduce its representatives attending the inspection and to present an overview of its pharmacovigilance system, and clarifying with the sponsor any anticipated difficulties relating to the conduct of the inspection.

rows.review_note: Review: Title reworded to say "may" (Permitted). Double-check: confirmed against source.

f.title: At the closing meeting, the sponsor may correct misconceptions and misunderstandings in the findings
f.statement: The purposes of the closing meeting include summarising the inspection findings so the sponsor clearly understands the outcomes, defining the grading of any deficiencies identified, explaining the procedures and timelines for distribution of the inspection report, the sponsor's response and any follow-up measures, and giving the sponsor an opportunity to correct any misconceptions and misunderstandings in the findings.

f.title: Close-out record content: deficiencies, root cause, CAPA, corrections, objective evidence and proposed completion dates
f.statement: TGA issues a close-out record with the inspection report to incorporate the sponsor's CAPA commitments and TGA's assessment of the CAPA. The close-out record documents any deficiencies identified, the root cause of the deficiencies, the proposed corrective and preventative actions to the root cause, corrections to observed examples (if relevant), objective evidence provided (if relevant), proposed completion dates of CAPAs, any comments by the inspector and the final response acceptance.

f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Audit & inspection readiness

f.title: Follow-up continues until a CAPA plan that addresses the identified non-compliance is completed
f.statement: When non-compliance with Australian pharmacovigilance legislation and guidelines is identified during an inspection, follow-up will be required until a CAPA plan that appropriately addresses the non-compliance is completed.
f.applicability: Inspections that identify non-compliance with Australian pharmacovigilance legislation and guidelines
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: Sponsor (sponsor of medicines included on the ARTG)
rows.quote: When non-compliance with Australian pharmacovigilance legislation and guidelines is identified during an inspection, follow-up will be required until a CAPA plan that appropriately addresses the non-compliance is completed.

f.title: TGA may initiate follow-up actions such as meetings, progress reports, re-inspection, data requests, PI variations and safety communications
f.statement: Follow-up actions TGA may initiate, as appropriate, include meeting the sponsor to discuss the deficiencies, their impact and its action plans; reviewing progress reports on the corrective actions; re-inspecting to assess implementation of the CAPA plan; asking the sponsor to provide data it has not yet submitted; requesting variations to amend product information documents; impact analyses (for example following a review of data not previously included); asking the sponsor to issue safety communications or amend marketing and/or advertising information; communicating the inspection findings to other regulatory authorities where applicable under international agreements; and taking other product-related actions depending on the impact of the deficiencies and the outcome of follow-up.

f.title: Significant or critical PV non-compliance can lead to ARTG cancellation or suspension and prosecution
f.statement: If TGA identifies significant or critical deviations where the sponsor fails to comply with pharmacovigilance requirements, TGA can cancel or suspend medicines from the ARTG for refusing or failing to comply with a condition of registration or listing (subsections 29D(1)(b) and 30(2)(c) of the Act), prosecute offences related to not complying with conditions of registration or listing (section 21A of the Act), and prosecute offences related to not complying with requirements to notify TGA of adverse effects (section 29A of the Act).
f.legal_basis: Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 s29D(1)(b), s30(2)(c), s21A, s29A
